Package org.rcmd.jneuroformats

Class Nifti1

java.lang.Object
org.rcmd.jneuroformats.Nifti1
public class Nifti1 extends Object
Class representing a volume stored in NIfTI-1 format. Only standard-compliant single-file NIfTI (.nii and .nii.gz) files are supported. The FreeSurfer "hack" of storing surface data in NIfTI files is explicitly not supported. The volume data is stored in an FsMgh instance (with an FsMghHeader and FsMghData), which makes converting between NIfTI and the FreeSurfer MGH/MGZ formats straightforward: read a NIfTI file with read(Path) and get the volume as an FsMgh via toMgh(), or wrap an existing FsMgh via fromMgh(FsMgh) and write it out with write(Path).

    • read

      public static Nifti1 read(Path filePath) throws IOException, FileNotFoundException
      Read a file in NIfTI-1 format and return a Nifti1 object. The file format is determined from the file extension (.nii or .nii.gz).
      Parameters:
      filePath - the name of the file to read, as a Path object.
      Returns:
      a Nifti1 object.
      Throws:
      IOException - if IO error occurs.
      FileNotFoundException - if the file does not exist.
      See Also:
      • if you want to read a file and specify the format.

    • extractRas

      protected static void extractRas(Nifti1Header h, FsMghHeader mghHeader)
      Extract the voxel-to-world (RAS) transform from a NIfTI-1 header into an MGH header. Prefers the sform (per the NIfTI-1 standard); falls back to the qform.
      Parameters:
      h - the NIfTI-1 header.
      mghHeader - the MGH header to fill.

      protected static void readData(ByteBuffer buf, FsMgh mgh, float slope, float inter) throws IOException
      Read the voxel data from a NIfTI file and apply scaling.
      Parameters:
      buf - the buffer, positioned at the start of the voxel data.
      mgh - the volume to fill.

      inter - the scaling intercept.

    • writeData

      protected static void writeData(ByteBuffer buf, FsMgh mgh) throws IOException
      Write the voxel data from an FsMgh volume to a ByteBuffer, in NIfTI order (the last dimension varies fastest, same as in MGH).
